Pt 8 for tracking and Pt 10 for everything else! I used to use cubase, but all the studios in my area run pro-tools, so I don't get a lot of choice. Editing also feels a little more intuitive compared to other programs I've tried.

(i meant to say that pro-tools is more intuitive for editing)The drum room I tend to work out of runs 8, My home studio runs 10. I find 8 is a little more stable, but 10 has a few tiny differences that suit my workflow when it comes time to edit

cubase is great for people who run a lot of synths or programmed drums, It has a great drum map and is pretty good for tracking audio, but just not good compared to pro-tools. plus my clients are mostly rock, punk and metal, so I program few things, and don't need a fancy drum-map

Yeah certainly the editing tools being color coded so you know which one is active and always right there towards the top left are pretty intuitive now that I think about it. I've been using protools 8 since I had a sony vaio! Pro tools was never known for it's stability as far as I know but it has crashed on me very few times and thankfully never after any important changes were made.

I use Ableton Live. I use it because I know the program very well. It's great to get musical idea's down in its session mode and is just an amazing program for production and sound design. I will also use it to mix. I don't put much on the master buss. Just an EQ, Mixbuss Compressor, a limiter, and sometimes a multiband compressor/limiter. I figure that the mix is what should sound great and mastering should only be used to control the overall dynamic range and frequency balance. That's all mastering is imo. Ableton Live is an amazing program and if you haven't tried, I highly suggest you check out their youtube page and see what its about. I've tried all the major DAW's on the market and I would say Cubase is a close second, and fl studio would be my third. Bitwig studio is an amazing DAW as well, its still version 1 and needs a lot more updates but if you're looking for something to get crazy with in regards to sound design, Bitwig is a monster.

get crazy with in regards to sound design

Can you elaborate? What do you mean?

Bitwig has really great modulation devices you can use to help create interesting sounds. Ableton Live also offers a ton of great devices with Max4Live. Here's a few expamples of the modulation devices Bitwig has to offer.

XY Effect Container LFO Mod Device Step Mod

If you have an interest in Bitwig I highly suggest you check out this user's channel. If you watch his videos in sequence from beginning to end you can learn Bitwig in no time. It also supports Linux which is really cool for any Linux users. It's in version 1 and has come out with some amazing updates. I feel it will be a force to be reckoned within a few years on the DAW market. I guess the only draw back for me is their audio metering system, its kind of weird and also the quantization is a bit weird. I wasn't able to undo any kind of quantization i was doing. Those aren't major issues and when version 1.5 (if it has corrected those issues) comes out. I will definitely be using it more.

I was at six flags with my boys today ( eight year old twins and a six year old ). We were having a grand ol' time ' til we exited the Titan. One of my twins fell through a gap between the roller coaster and the platform. I freaked the fuck out. All I heard was a collective gasp, then absolutely nothing, as I looked down and screamed his name. The scariest feeling I ever experienced, and I wish it on no one. I couldn't see him. All I could see was a metal grate and some sort of rail around ten feet below, then the ground thirty or forty feet below that. Someone yells that they see him. Now I see him, too. He's startled but he's alive. His twin is crying and pounding his little chest in fear. They bring him to me and everybody scatters. I take him to first aid, where they look him over, give him some ice, and send us on our way. So I took him to real doctor to make sure everything really is ok. HIs arms and legs and back are scraped, his chin is bruised, but other than that he's fine. A little while later his twin tells me he would have shot himself if his brother had died. I didn't know how to respond. I still haven't responded, except to give him a big hug. It was a very scary episode and I thank you for letting me talk about it.
